**Advancement profile integrity fix**

Closed a gap where one advancement could be recorded to your cross-world profile from a Free Play run, and where a related command was unreachable without cheats. Nothing earned in Free Play is written to your profile now, and the ordering the advancement tree implies is enforced against what you have actually earned, not what a command can grant.

**Deleting custom editor content now cleans up after itself**

Those leftovers kept influencing what the train generated, and the next thing you saved under the same name inherited them. A delete now takes the whole template with it.

- Deleting editor content removes its sidecars, spawn weight and sub-variant group membership
- A name you reuse after a delete starts clean instead of inheriting the old template's settings

### 0.830.0

**The CurseForge modpack catches up on its own**

The CurseForge modpack is built around that release's Dungeon Train file, and CurseForge rejects a pack that points at a file it has not approved yet. The pipeline already waited for approval — but when approval took longer than it was willing to wait, which turned out to be most of the time, that release was simply never added to the pack, and nothing ever tried again. The CurseForge pack had quietly fallen forty releases behind the Modrinth one. A scheduled check now looks every few hours for the newest release whose file CurseForge has since approved, and publishes the pack for it. A slow approval is a delay of a few hours now, not a missing version.

- The CurseForge modpack no longer falls behind when CurseForge is slow to approve a file
- Slow approvals are picked up automatically within a few hours — no manual re-run needed
- The pack is brought up to the newest release; older gaps are left as they are

- Traps now appear in the Overworld stretch, and no longer in Chunks

### 0.827.0

**Train Editor no longer drags the tick rate down**

Standing at a plot in the Train Editor, especially a Contents group parent, used to cost the server most of its tick budget: the editor was re-checking which pack every template came from on disk every tick, and rebuilding the whole contents registry for every plot lookup. Both are now cached, so the editor ticks at full speed with hundreds of plots stamped. A new "traps" contents group with four members rides along, gated to the Void, Upside Down and Chunks stretches of the line.

- Editor overlay cost at a Contents group plot: 85–180 ms per tick → about 3 ms
- Template provenance (yours / imported / bundled) is cached and refreshes immediately on save, delete, rename, import or pack switch

- Observers stay silent while a carriage is placed, lifted onto the train, and furnished
- Also applies when a template opens in the editor or builder, and when a saved train reloads

Now a glide only counts while you are actually inside a carriage — down a corridor still counts, skimming the roof does not — and the moment you land, everything resumes from where you left off with nothing paid out for the flight.
